title: Buy lunch to take away
subtitle: Buy lunch to take away
outcome: Order a slice of quiche to take away and request heating.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais un sandwich au fromage.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a cheese sandwich.

vocabulary.note: Fillings vary; ask if ingredients matter.

vocabulary.example: Une part de quiche, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.note: Used for a portion cut from a larger food.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does the set lunch deal include a drink?
vocabulary.note: Contents depend on the bakery.

vocabulary.example: C’est à emporter, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.note: Service phrase. Sur place means to eat on the premises.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you heat up my quiche?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Use after pouvez in a request.

dialogue.target: Une part de quiche, à emporter, s’il vous plaît.
dialogue.meaning: A slice of quiche to take away, please.

dialogue.target: Vous voulez une formule avec une boisson ?
dialogue.meaning: Would you like a set deal with a drink?

dialogue.target: Non, merci. Vous pouvez réchauffer la quiche ?
dialogue.meaning: No, thank you. Can you heat up the quiche?
Yes, I’ll heat it up.

grammar.title: Ask someone to do something
grammar.explanation: Vous pouvez + infinitive is an ordinary polite request: Vous pouvez réchauffer… ? Keep the action verb in its infinitive form.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for this meaning.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “Can you heat up the quiche?”
sentenceActivity.explanation: Pouvez is conjugated for vous; réchauffer stays in the infinitive.

title: Find products in a shop
subtitle: Find products in a shop
outcome: Locate a shop section and find a basket and checkout.

vocabulary.example: Le rayon des surgelés est au fond.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The frozen-food section is at the back.
vocabulary.note: Rayon means a department or product section here.

vocabulary.example: Je prends un panier pour mes courses.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m taking a basket for my shopping.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche le rayon des surgelés.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for the frozen-food section.
vocabulary.note: Use chercher + the thing sought; no pour.

vocabulary.example: Les pâtes sont au fond du magasin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The pasta is at the back of the shop.
vocabulary.note: Location phrase; au combines à and le.

dialogue.target: Je cherche le rayon des surgelés.
dialogue.meaning: I’m looking for the frozen-food section.

dialogue.target: Il est au fond, près des caisses.
dialogue.meaning: It’s at the back, near the checkouts.
And where are the baskets?
At the entrance, on the right.

grammar.title: Where is and where are
grammar.explanation: Où est… ? asks for one place or item. Où sont… ? asks for a plural: Où sont les surgelés ? The accent distinguishes où (where) from ou (or).

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for this meaning.

sentenceActivity.hint: Use sont with the plural les surgelés.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Où asks where. Les surgelés is plural, so use sont rather than est.

title: Finish the meal
subtitle: Finish the meal
outcome: Request missing tableware, split payment and ask for a receipt.

vocabulary.note: Use after pouvez in a request.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir une autre serviette ?
vocabulary.note: At a table this is a napkin; elsewhere it can mean a towel.
Not the restaurant menu.
Adverb. Ask whether the restaurant can split payment.
Here a payment receipt, not a transport ticket.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir un autre couteau ?
vocabulary.note: Plural: des couteaux.

dialogue.meaning: I’m missing a fork.
I’ll bring you one.

dialogue.target: Merci. Et nous pouvons payer séparément ?
dialogue.meaning: Thank you. And can we pay separately?
Yes, of course.

dialogue.target: Je paie par carte. Je peux avoir un ticket ?
dialogue.meaning: I’m paying by card. Can I have a receipt?
Yes, here is your receipt.

grammar.title: Pouvoir for practical requests
grammar.explanation: Je peux… ? means Can I…? Nous pouvons… ? means Can we…? Follow pouvoir with an infinitive such as payer or avoir.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for this meaning.

sentenceActivity.explanation: Rising intonation turns this word order into an ordinary spoken question. Payer stays in the infinitive.

title: Ask about a rental
subtitle: Ask about a rental
outcome: Check rent and included charges before reading a tenancy agreement.

vocabulary.example: Le loyer est de huit cents euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The rent is eight hundred euros.

vocabulary.note: Ask what is included; arrangements vary.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to read the tenancy agreement.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des baux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to call the landlord.
vocabulary.note: Feminine: la propriétaire. Here the owner who rents out the home; not a statement about legal responsibilities.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to move in on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: One move into a new home; déménager means move home.
Adjective: meublé for appartement; meublée with a feminine noun.
Feminine: une locataire.

dialogue.meaning: What is the monthly rent?
Eight hundred euros, including service charges.
Which service charges are included?
Water and building maintenance.

dialogue.target: Je voudrais lire le bail avant d’emménager.
dialogue.meaning: I would like to read the tenancy agreement before moving in.
Of course, I’ll send it to you.

grammar.title: Ask which costs are included
grammar.explanation: Quelles agrees with feminine plural charges. Comprises also agrees with charges. Learn Les charges sont comprises ? as a practical question, then ask what those charges cover.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for this meaning.

sentenceActivity.hint: Use sont after the plural charges.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Comprises takes feminine plural agreement with charges.

title: Organise a working day
subtitle: Organise a working day
outcome: Discuss a meeting, a deadline and a task that matters first.

vocabulary.example: La réunion commence à quatorze heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The meeting starts at two p.m.
vocabulary.note: Workplace sense.

vocabulary.example: Mon horaire de travail change lundi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My work schedule changes on Monday.
vocabulary.note: Here the organisation of working hours. Les horaires de travail is the usual plural phrase for working hours; the noun is masculine.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le délai pour répondre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How long do we have to reply?
vocabulary.note: A period of time, not always a specific due date.

vocabulary.example: Je commence cette tâche ce matin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am starting this task this morning.
vocabulary.note: Keep the circumflex: tache without it means a stain.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to finish before noon.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; can take an object directly.
Adjective: urgente with a feminine noun.

dialogue.target: La réunion est à quelle heure ?
dialogue.meaning: What time is the meeting?

dialogue.target: À quatorze heures. Tu peux terminer cette tâche avant ?
dialogue.meaning: At two p.m. Can you finish this task before then?
Yes. Is it urgent?

dialogue.target: Oui, le client attend une réponse avant midi.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, the customer is waiting for a reply before noon.

dialogue.target: D’accord, je vais terminer ce matin.
dialogue.meaning: All right, I am going to finish this morning.

grammar.title: Near future
grammar.explanation: Aller in the present + an infinitive describes a plan: je vais terminer. After tu peux, keep terminer in its dictionary form: tu peux terminer cette tâche. Tu is used between colleagues who already use familiar forms.

pictureActivity.prompt: Choose the French for this meaning.

sentenceActivity.prompt: Build: “I am going to finish this task.”
sentenceActivity.hint: Use Je vais, then the action.
sentenceActivity.explanation: Terminer stays in the infinitive. Cette agrees with feminine tâche.
